CHARACTER FACIAL EXPRESSIONS AND ACTING — PRODUCTION STANDARD

Irreverents \| 2026-11-23 09:13 AM EST \| Owner-directed visual improvement

Status: PRODUCTION QUALITY TARGET, not a new game mechanic. All new art is approved for iterative use by default; no owner sign-off needed.

# WHY THIS EXISTS

The owner likes the current A00 visual direction, the P01 starter sprite pack and the subsequent P02 source sheets, but wants CHARACTER FACES TO BE SIGNIFICANTLY MORE EXPRESSIVE, in the spirit of the personality and immediate readability of Kirby animation. This means expressive face ACTING—not copying Kirby's round body, copyrighted design, named powers, or existing sprite art. Small expressive changes should make characters charming, comical and unmistakably emotionally alive.

# THE ACTING GOAL

At actual game size, a character's eyes, mouth, head direction and posture communicate a clear emotional beat BEFORE the player has time to inspect fine detail. Faces must change with the action, not remain identical dots through idle, attack, jump, hurt and victory. Preserve the appealing simple face—no need for realistic facial anatomy, text balloons, elaborate anime eyes, or noisy expressions.

A good character is recognizable when reduced to a silhouette; a great game character is recognizable by silhouette AND emotionally readable at a glance.

# FACE SHAPE VOCABULARY

Eyes: widen / squash / narrow / look sideways / glance up; make differing intent visibly readable. Brow/eyelid contour: slight compression or tilt can convey concentration, surprise, alarm or comic suspicion. Mouth: smile, grin, tiny open gasp, determined line, delighted laugh, effort shout, clenched grimace. Cheeks/head pose: slight cheek/blush shifts, head tip, recoil or squash/stretch can amplify the face when the pixel count is tiny. Do not rely on color alone: shape matters.

All expressions must preserve the SAME character identity, face placement, palette, original styling, perspective and readability. Avoid suddenly changing a face's eye separation/proportions or turning the hero into a different species.

If the native face is too small for eyebrows or detailed mouths, use bolder eyes, contrasting simple mouth and HEAD/POSE changes. Do not invent tiny unreadable pixels.

# CHARACTER EXPRESSION BEATS TO DESIGN AND TEST (RECOMMENDED PRODUCTION CHECKLIST)

Idle: curious/open/friendly neutral expression; optional spontaneous blink or small quirky look.

Walk: lively interested or mischievous expression, with subtle eye direction.

Run/dash: determined focus and wind-up grin, eyes narrowed just enough to read.

Jump: anticipation/effort followed by open-eyed lift or playful delight.

Attack: unmistakable effort expression (grit, open mouth or compressed brow), intensity matches attack timing.

Grab / lift / throw: exertion, strain and delicious comic determination; celebratory reaction after a spectacular throw.

Crouch / stealth: lowered brows, watchful sideways eyes and compressed mouth.

Surprised / alarmed: widened eyes and simple open mouth, clear at 1×.

Hurt / stunned: squeezed eyes, wincing mouth, strong head recoil.

Win / delighted reaction: genuine beaming smile, sparkling delight, laughing eyes, or character-specific cheeky victory smirk.

These are a facial ACTING vocabulary, not a hard requirement to add unused gameplay states to every character today. Prioritize currently implemented actions and expand states incrementally.

# DISTINCT CHARACTERS NEED DISTINCT EXPRESSIVE PERSONALITIES

Two characters reacting to the SAME event should not be cosmetic recolors of the same face. E.g. brave scout might grin during danger, squint when dashing and make a startled wide-eyed face after a knockback; cautious rogue might smirk when sneaking, glance sideways when discovered and show a shocked grimace on defeat. These are illustrative personalities, not final roster lore.

Villains and civilians should have their own face language consistent with the confirmed exactly three authored NPC modes. Mode 1 expected-role normal behavior can remain happy—even while fighting when appropriate; good-guy mode 2 confusion/distress must read clearly; mode 3 blinding rage must be striking. Villain enemy alarm signaling may occur in mode 1; don't add a narrative distress requirement. NO NPC AI.

# P01 → P03 CHARACTER UPGRADE DIRECTION

P01 is legitimate prototype-ready separated art, but its faces across its seven states are too similar. Improve the CURRENT named hero art WITHOUT reverting to low-quality rectangle characters or treating P02 flattened image sheets as ready sprites. Recommended next output is P03 character face-acting pass:

- At least a compact A/B comparison of old and new hero poses at exactly their actual rendered iPhone gameplay size (320×180 reference).

- Several visibly different facial reactions in implemented moves; show a simple face-expression contact row per hero. Be selective and consistent with character shape.

- Provide actual transparent RGBA frames or face-overlay layers that cleanly align to current hero animation cells, plus matching atlas/manifest and anchors; preserve current code compatibility or include exact migration notes.

- Test blink, surprise, focused dash, attack effort, hurt and happy response where corresponding gameplay events exist. Example count is a QA target, not a locked game content requirement.

- For genuine animation, eyes/mouth/eyebrows can change during the motion rather than being a single static expression stamped on every frame. Head and body pose should support the change.

- Show in a short animated GIF and a common 320×180 level mock, if feasible; inspect actual native PNGs, not an AI-generated review illustration.

- Keep colors coherent and favor simplicity; personality first, detail second.

- Route new artifacts into Drive P03 or later functional production folder with a clear README, direct indexed links, version, and brief QA evidence; do not overwrite P01 without ensuring Claude can upgrade safely.

# DO NOT MISLABEL COMPLETION

An attractive poster of seven expressions on a checkerboard background is SOURCE ART, not seven transparent production frames until extracted and verified. A static expression collage with nearly identical mouths is not a meaningful upgrade. Never claim motion, technical importability or engine deployment based on an image-generation board alone.

Default use permission means producer and Claude can implement the best current art immediately, THEN improve it. The user need not approve each face.

# FUTURE SESSION STARTUP RULE

Before ANY playable-character/NPC sprite request, open this spec, relevant A00 sources and the root asset catalog. Include expressive face acting as a required visible quality target and preserve the player experience on iPhone. After real delivery, update the root catalog, request and shared changelog; log exact file routes.
